plan.headline: 6 dates in the Northeast and Ontario: Burlington and Portland lead, plus four markets they skipped on the big fall tour
plan.summary: Last fall's tour played every big Northeast market (NYC, Philly, Boston, DC, Pittsburgh, Buffalo, Albany, Providence, Toronto), and their radius clauses rule out most of the high-affinity towns close to NYC. This run goes around them: NYC to Harrisburg, Syracuse, Kingston, Ottawa, Burlington, Portland ME. Every leg is 4.6 hours or less and no two stops are within 120 km of each other or of a played city. Burlington (affinity 0.988, opportunity +0.74) and Portland ME (0.971, +0.22) are the data-backed anchors. The four others are routing stops that keep the van under 6 hours a day. Their Qloo scores weren't in the heatmap's top tier, so pitch them as fill-in markets, not proven ones. Oklahoma and West Michigan score higher but can't be reached under the drive limit.

stops.why: First leg out of NYC (3.6 hours). About 150 km from Philly and 170 km from Scranton, so it clears both radius clauses that block Lancaster and Easton (affinity 0.986 and 0.99). It's the nearest open city to that high-affinity central PA area.

risks: Room size mismatch: last fall they played Brooklyn Steel, Union Transfer, Thalia Hall (2 nights) and Hollywood Palladium. Those are 1,000+ cap rooms. 150-400 rooms in Burlington and Portland could sell out in minutes and leave money on the table. Ask for holds on the bigger rooms there (Higher Ground ballroom, State Theatre).

Only Burlington and Portland ME have strong Qloo affinity numbers. Harrisburg, Syracuse, Kingston and Ottawa weren't in the heatmap's top tier, so they're routing stops with unproven demand. Keep guarantees modest.
Qloo returned no age or gender data for this artist, so 21+ vs all-ages is a guess. Check venue age policies, especially campus-heavy Syracuse and Kingston.
Kingston's only small-room match is The Grad Club, and there's no backup venue.
Two border crossings (into Canada after Syracuse, back into the US before Burlington). Sort out work permits and gear carnets for the Canadian dates early.
The opener lists include off-genre names (The Try Guys, Nia Sioux, Steven Furtick). Ignore those. The picks here are the indie/shoegaze matches only.
